name: STM32F103C8T6
title: Medium-density performance line Arm Cortex-M3 MCU, 64 or 128 KB Flash, USB, CAN, 7 timers, 2 ADCs, 9 interfaces
summary: A 32-bit Arm Cortex-M3 microcontroller family running to 72 MHz from 2.0 V to 3.6 V, with 64 KB (x8) or 128 KB (xB) of Flash and 20 KB of SRAM. It carries two 12-bit 1 µs ADCs, a 7-channel DMA, a motor-control timer with three general-purpose 16-bit timers, two watchdogs, an RTC on a VBAT domain, and up to two I2C, three USARTs, two SPIs, CAN and full-speed USB. Packages run from VFQFPN36 to LQFP100 and the BGAs, for -40 °C to 85 °C or 105 °C. The STM32F103C8T6 is the LQFP48 part with 64 KB of Flash, 37 I/Os, for -40 °C to 85 °C.
key_figures: 64 KB (x8) or 128 KB (xB) / 20 KB; C8T6: 64 KB / 20 KB
VDD 2.0 V to 3.6 V; VDDA 2.4 V min with ADC; VBAT 1.8 V to 3.6 V
36 mA typ at 72 MHz from Flash, peripherals on (VDD = 3.3 V); 50.0 mA max at 85 °C, 50.3 mA at 105 °C
Stop 14 µA typ (regulator low-power, 3.3 V); Standby 2 µA typ
2 × 12-bit, 1 µs, up to 16 channels (C8T6: 10), 0 V to VREF+
HSE 4 MHz to 16 MHz, HSI 8 MHz, LSI 40 kHz, LSE 32.768 kHz, PLL to 72 MHz
26/37/51/80 by package, most 5 V tolerant; ±8 mA (±20 mA relaxed)
up to 2 × I2C, 3 × USART (4.5 Mbit/s), 2 × SPI (18 Mbit/s), CAN 2.0B, USB 2.0 FS, SWD/JTAG
VFQFPN36, LQFP48, UFQFPN48, LQFP64, TFBGA64, LQFP100, LFBGA100, UFBGA100

notes: An order code adds the package letter (T LQFP, U VFQFPN or UFQFPN, H BGA, I UFBGA) and the temperature digit (6: -40 °C to 85 °C, 7: -40 °C to 105 °C), e.g. STM32F103C8T6.

operation.text: Cortex-M3 at up to 72 MHz (1.25 DMIPS/MHz with zero-wait memory) with single-cycle multiply and hardware divide; 64 KB or 128 KB Flash and 20 KB SRAM; 2.0 V to 3.6 V supply; POR, PDR and PVD; 4 MHz to 16 MHz crystal oscillator, factory-trimmed 8 MHz RC, 40 kHz RC, PLL, and 32 kHz oscillator for the RTC; Sleep, Stop and Standby with a VBAT domain; two 12-bit 1 µs ADCs with up to 16 channels and dual sample-and-hold; 7-channel DMA; up to 80 I/Os, nearly all 5 V tolerant, each able to raise an external interrupt; SWD and JTAG; seven timers; up to two I2C, three USARTs, two SPIs (18 Mbit/s), a CAN 2.0B and a full-speed USB device; CRC unit and 96-bit unique ID.

The STM32F103x8 (64 KB) and STM32F103xB (128 KB) are the medium-density members of the STM32F103 performance line, pin and software compatible with the low- and high-density members and with the STM32F101 and STM32F102 lines. T parts come in VFQFPN36, C parts in LQFP48 and UFQFPN48, R parts in LQFP64 and TFBGA64, V parts in LQFP100, LFBGA100 and UFBGA100. Suffix 6 is -40 °C to 85 °C, suffix 7 -40 °C to 105 °C ambient. The STM32F103C8T6 is the LQFP48 part with 64 KB Flash, -40 °C to 85 °C, with 37 I/Os, 2 SPI, 2 I2C, 3 USART, USB, CAN and 10 ADC channels.

Flash of 64 KB or 128 KB holds code and data; 20 KB of SRAM reads and writes at the CPU clock with no wait states. The CRC unit computes a CRC of 32-bit words with a fixed polynomial, which can check the Flash contents at run time.

The address space is split into eight blocks, 0 to 7. Block 0 holds the code area: Flash, or Flash or system memory aliased at the bottom according to the BOOT pins, plus system memory and the option bytes. Block 1 is SRAM, block 2 the peripherals, block 7 the Cortex-M3 internal peripherals. The APB space holds, from the top: CRC, Flash interface, RCC, DMA, USART1, SPI1, TIM1, ADC2, ADC1, ports E to A, EXTI, AFIO, PWR, BKP, bxCAN, the 512-byte SRAM shared by USB and CAN, the USB registers, I2C2, I2C1, USART3, USART2, SPI2, IWDG, WWDG, RTC, TIM4, TIM3 and TIM2.

The NVIC handles 43 maskable interrupt channels (on top of the 16 Cortex-M3 lines) with 16 priority levels, tail-chaining and automatic state saving. The EXTI has 19 edge-detect lines, each selectable for rising, falling or both edges and separately maskable; up to 80 GPIOs map onto its 16 external lines. It catches pulses shorter than an APB2 clock period.

Reset starts the core on the 8 MHz HSI RC. A 4 MHz to 16 MHz HSE can be chosen and is watched by the clock security system: on its failure the system falls back to HSI and can raise an interrupt. Prescalers set AHB and APB2 to 72 MHz max and APB1 to 36 MHz max. With HSI feeding the PLL the system clock tops out at 64 MHz. USB needs HSE and the PLL running, with USBCLK at 48 MHz. A 1 µs ADC conversion needs APB2 at 14, 28 or 56 MHz. Timers on an APB bus run at twice its clock when its prescaler is not 1. MCO can output PLLCLK/2, HSI, HSE or SYSCLK.
At startup the boot pins choose user Flash, system memory or embedded SRAM. The bootloader in system memory reprograms the Flash over USART1.

VDD, 2.0 V to 3.6 V, feeds the I/Os and the internal regulator. VDDA and VSSA, 2.0 V to 3.6 V (2.4 V minimum when the ADC runs), feed the ADC, reset blocks, RC oscillators and PLL, and connect to VDD and VSS. VBAT, 1.8 V to 3.6 V, feeds the RTC, the 32 kHz oscillator and the backup registers through a switch when VDD is absent.

Power-on and power-down reset are always active and hold the chip in reset below VPOR/PDR (about 1.9 V), so no external reset circuit is needed. The PVD, enabled by software, compares VDD/VDDA with a threshold set by PLS[2:0] from about 2.2 V to 2.9 V and can interrupt on crossing it in either direction.
The regulator runs in main mode in Run, low-power mode in Stop, and powers down in Standby, where its output goes high impedance and register and SRAM contents are lost. It is on after every reset.
Only the CPU stops; peripherals keep running and any interrupt or event wakes it.

All clocks of the 1.8 V domain stop and the PLL, HSI and HSE are off, while SRAM and registers keep their contents; the regulator can be in normal or low-power mode. Wakeup comes from any EXTI line: the 16 external ones, the PVD, an RTC alarm, or a USB wakeup.

The regulator is off, so the whole 1.8 V domain loses power along with PLL, HSI and HSE; only the backup domain and standby circuitry keep their state. Exit is by an NRST or IWDG reset, an RTC alarm, or WKUP going high. The RTC, the IWDG and their clocks keep running in Stop and Standby.

Seven channels move data between any mix of memory and peripherals, with circular buffers, a hardware request per channel plus software trigger, and independent source and destination widths. SPI, I2C, USART, the timers and the ADC can use it.

The RTC and ten 16-bit backup registers (20 bytes) are fed from VDD when present, otherwise from VBAT. The RTC has a 32-bit counter with an alarm compare register, a periodic interrupt, and a 20-bit prescaler that by default turns 32.768 kHz into a 1 s tick. Its clock is the LSE crystal, the 40 kHz LSI or HSE/128. A 512 Hz output allows calibration against crystal error.

TIM1 is an advanced-control timer: four channels for input capture, output compare, edge- or centre-aligned PWM and one-pulse output, three of them with complementary outputs and programmable dead time, plus emergency-stop (break) input; in debug its counter can freeze and its outputs switch off. TIM2, TIM3 and TIM4 are 16-bit up/down timers with a 16-bit prescaler and four channels each (up to 12 captures/compares/PWM on the largest packages), handle quadrature encoders and up to three Hall sensors, and chain with TIM1 and each other. All four can request DMA.

The independent watchdog has a 12-bit down-counter with an 8-bit prescaler on the 40 kHz LSI, runs in Stop and Standby, and is enabled by hardware or software through the option bytes. The window watchdog has a 7-bit down-counter on the main clock with an early-warning interrupt. SysTick is a 24-bit auto-reload down-counter with a selectable clock, meant for an OS. Both watchdog counters can freeze in debug.

Up to two I2C interfaces work as master or slave in standard and fast modes, with 7-bit dual slave addressing, 7- or 10-bit addressing as master, hardware CRC, DMA, and SMBus 2.0/PMBus support. The SDA and SCL pins are not true open-drain: the PMOS to VDD is switched off but still present.
One USART reaches 4.5 Mbit/s and the others 2.25 Mbit/s. All have CTS/RTS flow control, IrDA SIR, ISO 7816 smartcard and LIN master/slave modes, and can use DMA.
Up to two SPIs at up to 18 Mbit/s, master or slave, full duplex or simplex, 8- or 16-bit frames, a 3-bit prescaler for eight master clock rates, hardware CRC for SD/MMC modes, and DMA.

The CAN controller meets 2.0A and 2.0B (active) at up to 1 Mbit/s, with 11-bit and 29-bit identifiers, three transmit mailboxes, two three-deep receive FIFOs and 14 scalable filter banks. It shares a 512-byte SRAM with USB, and its pins are shared with USB (PA11/PA12).

A full-speed (12 Mbit/s) USB device with software-configured endpoints and suspend/resume, USB-IF certified. Its 48 MHz clock comes from the PLL, which must run from the HSE crystal. D+ (USBDP) needs a 1.5 kΩ pull-up to 3.0 V to 3.6 V; USB works down to 2.7 V with degraded electrical performance.

Each GPIO can be a push-pull or open-drain output, an input (floating, pulled up or pulled down), or be handed to an alternate function. All are high-current capable. The alternate-function configuration can be locked. I/Os on APB2 toggle at up to 18 MHz.

Each GPIO sinks or sources up to ±8 mA, or ±20 mA with relaxed VOL/VOH; PC13, PC14 and PC15 only ±3 mA, at no more than 2 MHz into 30 pF. The total sourced by all I/Os plus the run current stays within IVDD (150 mA), and the total sunk within IVSS (150 mA).

All I/Os are both CMOS and TTL compliant without configuration. Standard I/Os meet the CMOS levels (VIH 0.65 VDD, VIL 0.35 VDD, tested in production) and, from VDD of about 2.16 V up, the TTL levels (VIH 2 V, VIL 0.8 V); the design-simulation thresholds follow the VIL/VIH equations, for example VIH 1.96 V and VIL 1.25 V at VDD = 3.6 V for standard I/Os, 1.67 V and 1 V for FT I/Os.

Two 12-bit ADCs share up to 16 external channels, convert in single-shot or scan mode, and can sample simultaneously or interleaved, or in single-shunt mode. An analog watchdog interrupts when one, several or all channels leave a programmed window. TIM1 to TIM4 events can trigger regular and injected conversions and DMA. Calibrate after every power-up. VREF+ is joined to VDDA (and VREF- to VSSA) in the VFQFPN and LQFP packages.

The source resistance RAIN is limited by the sampling time: 0.4 kΩ at 1.5 cycles up to 50 kΩ at 55.5 cycles with fADC = 14 MHz. Negative injection into an analog input disturbs conversions on other inputs; a Schottky diode from pin to ground is advised where it can occur.

The sensor gives a voltage linear in temperature (about 1.43 V at 25 °C, 4.3 mV/°C), read on ADC12_IN16 with VDDA from 2 V to 3.6 V. The internal reference VREFINT (1.20 V) is also readable by the ADC.

The SWJ-DP combines JTAG and serial-wire debug; SWDIO and SWCLK share pins with JTMS and JTCK, and a sequence on TMS switches between the two. After reset PA13, PA14, PA15, PB3 and PB4 are the debug pins.

Place the crystal and its load capacitors close to OSC_IN and OSC_OUT. Use high-quality ceramic CL1 and CL2 of 5 pF to 25 pF, normally equal, chosen so their series value plus about 10 pF of pin and board capacitance matches the crystal's load. HSE is characterized with a crystal of RS = 30 Ω and C = 30 pF; the internal feedback resistor is 200 kΩ.

Use high-quality ceramic CL1 and CL2 of 5 pF to 15 pF, normally equal. Keep CL1 and CL2 at 15 pF or less by choosing a crystal with a load capacitance of 7 pF or below; a 12.5 pF crystal is not to be used. Startup takes about 2.5 s at 25 °C and up to 60 s at -40 °C.

NRST has a CMOS input with Schmitt trigger, a 40 kΩ typical pull-up, and a filter that ignores pulses under 100 ns and passes pulses over 300 ns. A 0.1 µF capacitor to ground protects against parasitic resets; an external driver must take the pin below 0.8 V.
Each VDD pin gets 100 nF, with 4.7 µF on VDD_3; VDDA gets 10 nF plus 1 µF, as does VREF+ when it is fed separately. The 10 nF capacitors are good ceramics placed as close to the chip as possible.

ESD on any pin is class 2B and fast transient bursts on VDD/VSS class 4A at 72 MHz. Software should handle runaway conditions (corrupted program counter, unexpected reset, corrupted control registers); holding NRST or the oscillator pins low for 1 s reproduces the common failures for testing.

OSC32_IN, OSC32_OUT, PA4, PA5 and PC13 accept no injected current; FT pins accept -5 mA and no positive current; other pins ±5 mA, with no functional failure (ADC error above 5 LSB TUE, disturbance of neighbouring pins, resets, oscillator shift).

Voltages refer to VSS. Min and max values are guaranteed over temperature, supply and frequency by production test at 25 °C and TAmax on every part; values from characterization are mean ± 3σ. Typical values are at 25 °C, VDD = 3.3 V; typical ADC accuracy covers 95 % of parts (mean ± 2σ). Run-mode currents use code equivalent to Dhrystone 2.1 with all I/O pins static inputs, Flash wait states 0 up to 24 MHz, 1 up to 48 MHz and 2 above, and prefetch on; for the maximum tables fPCLK1 = fHCLK/2 and fPCLK2 = fHCLK, for the typical tables fPCLK1 = fHCLK/4, fPCLK2 = fHCLK/2 and fADCCLK = fPCLK2/4. Wakeup is measured with the 8 MHz HSI.

At TAmax = 82 °C with IDD 50 mA at 3.5 V (175 mW) and I/O loss of 272 mW (20 pins sinking 8 mA at 0.4 V, 8 sinking 20 mA at 1.3 V), PD is 447 mW and an LQFP100 (46 °C/W) reaches TJ = 102.6 °C, within suffix 6. At TAmax = 115 °C with 20 mA at 3.5 V (70 mW) and 64 mW of I/O loss, PD is 134 mW and TJ = 121.2 °C, which needs suffix 7.

The top carries the product identification (for example STM32F103CBT6 on the LQFP48), a date code (year and week) and a revision code; a pin-1 mark sits in one corner. Parts marked ES or E are engineering samples, not qualified for production.
